newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds trudge ahead in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds trudge ahead in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities took a breather from several days of active trade, plodding several ticks higher in quiet trade on Thursday.
Market participants lost inspiration after light mortgage banker selling hit the market earlier in the day, traders said.
One trader summed up the day's activity as "dealers chasing current coupons against new issue REMICs (Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduit securities)."
He said they were selling tranches from the REMICs they had hedged with passthrough securities or they were buying collateral to issue new REMICs.
Nevertheless, trading activity was subdued by customers' lack of enthusiasm.
"We saw some action in 7.0 and 7.5 percent coupons earlier on, but haven't seen any since," said another trader. "Now, it is extremely dead."
At about 1530EST/2030GMT, mortgages were up 2/32 to 5/32. Yield spreads to Treasuries widened modestly.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was up 3/32 at 99-27/32, yielding 98 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were up 3/32 at 99-23/32 and 99-28/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note ws up 7/32 at 99-11/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
